prompt: What does a pennant-shaped sign indicate?

decisions.prompt: The truck is slow. This sign is on the left and the yellow lines turn solid. What do you do?
decisions.signAlt: A yellow pennant-shaped sign, pointing right, on the left side of the road

wrongActions.label: Pass the truck now
wrongActions.consequence: A car came over the hill while you were in its lane. It had to swerve onto the shoulder to miss you.

wrongActions.label: Pass on the right shoulder
wrongActions.consequence: The shoulder is not a lane. You hit gravel, ran out of room at the guardrail and had to brake hard.

successText: You waited. A car came over the hill in the lane you would have been in. Once the line was broken again, you passed with a clear view.
ruleText: The pennant-shaped sign on the left side of the road marks the start of a no-passing zone: with a solid yellow line on your side, stay in your lane until the line is broken again.

citation.source: FHWA Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, 11th Edition
citation.section: Section 2C.53 (No Passing Zone sign, W14-3) and Section 3B.01 (yellow center line markings)

verified: Read in the FHWA PDFs, Nov 2026: the sign "shall be installed on the left-hand side of the roadway at the beginning of no-passing zones"; passing "is prohibited for traffic traveling adjacent to the solid line".
